VI.description: This example demonstrates how to continuously acquire buffered acceleration\2C sound pressure\2C or force measurements from IEPE sensors using a DAQmx device.\0A\0AFor instructions on how to connect your signals to the DAQ device\2C refer to your device documentation.

Constant.items: Finite Samples,Continuous Samples,Hardware Timed Single Point

Control.description: Logging Mode specifies whether to enable logging. \0A\0AIf you want to read data while logging\2C specify Log and Read mode.\0A\0AThere is also a Log Only mode which writes data to disk but does not return data to LabVIEW. Log Only mode is not included here but is shown in the Logging Advanced example.

Indicator.description: Actual Sample Rate returns the coerced value of the sample clock.\0A\0AIf using OnboardClock as your Sample Clock Source\2C your hardware will attempt to derive the sample clock from one of its internal timebases. If it is unable to derive the exact frequency you require\2C the rate will be coerced.

Control.description: Sample Clock Source specifies the source terminal of the Sample Clock.\0A\0ARefer to the Device Routes table in Measurement and Automation Explorer to determine eligible sample clock sources.
Sample Rate specifies the sampling rate in samples per channel per second. If you use an external source for the Sample Clock\2C set this input to the maximum expected rate of that clock.
TDMS File Path specifies the path to the TDMS file to which you want to log data.

The Task Type tab control selects which task type you wish to use. Depending on the tab that is currently selected\2C when you run the VI your task will configure the desired IEPE task type.\0A\0ANote that not all hardware supports IEPE excitation--refer to your device documentation for more info.

Physical Channel(s) specifies the names of the physical channels to use to create virtual channels. The DAQmx physical channel constant lists all physical channels on devices and modules installed in the system.\0A\0ATo specify a range of physical channels\2C use a colon between two channel numbers or two physical channel names\3A\0A Dev1/ai0\3A4\0A Dev1/ai0\3ADev1/ai4\0A\0AYou can specify channel ranges in reverse order\3A\0A Dev1/ai4\3A0\0A\0AUse commas to separate physical channel names and ranges in a list as follows\3A\0A Dev1/ai0\2C Dev1/ai3\3A6
Terminal Configuration specifies the input terminal configuration for the channel.
IEPE Current Value [A] specifies in amperes the amount of excitation to supply to the sensor. Refer to the sensor documentation to determine this value.
IEPE Excitation Source specifies the source of excitation.

Stop stops the acquisition.\0A\0AIt is recommended to stop your VI through this stop button so the DAQmx task can be properly cleared.

Control.description: Edge specifies on which edge of the digital signal to start acquiring or generating samples.

Digital Trigger Source specifies the name of a terminal where there is a digital signal to use as the source of the trigger.\0A\0ARefer to the Device Routes table in Measurement and Automation Explorer to determine eligible trigger sources.
Slope specifies on which slope of the signal to start acquiring or generating samples when the signal crosses the desired level.

Hysteresis adds a window above or below the trigger level and often is used to reduce false triggering due to noise or jitter in the signal. \0A\0AWhen using hysteresis with a rising slope\2C the trigger asserts when the signal starts below the trigger level minus hysteresis and then crosses above level. The trigger deasserts when the signal crosses below level minus hysteresis.

Level specifies at what threshold to start acquiring or generating samples. Specify this value in the units of the measurement or generation. Use slope to specify on which slope to trigger at this threshold.

Analog Trigger Source is the name of a virtual channel or terminal where there is an analog signal to use as the source of the trigger.\0A\0AIf you specify a virtual channel\2C all values will be in the engineering units (EU) of this virtual channel. If you specify a terminal\2C all values will be in volts (V). \0A\0ANot all hardware supports analog triggering. Refer to your device documentation for information on valid trigger sources. \0A\0ASome examples include\3A\0A APFI0\0A Dev1/ai0

Control.description: Pause Trigger Source specifies the name of a terminal where there is a digital signal to use as the source of the pause trigger. While the pause trigger is asserted\2C no sample clock edges will be registered.\0A\0ARefer to the Device Routes table in Measurement and Automation Explorer to determine eligible trigger sources.
Pause When specifies the state of the digital line that pauses the acquisition.

Control.description: Analog Pause Trigger Source is the name of a virtual channel or terminal where there is an analog signal to use as the source of the pause trigger.\0A\0AIf you specify a virtual channel\2C all values will be in the engineering units (EU) of this virtual channel. If you specify a terminal\2C all values will be in volts (V). \0A\0ANot all hardware supports analog triggering\2C and not all hardware supports pause triggering. Refer to your device documentation for information on valid trigger sources. \0A\0ASome examples include\3A\0A APFI0\0A Dev1/ai0
Pause When specifies to pause when the trigger source is above or below a specified level.

Level specifies the threshold at which to pause the task. Specify this value in the units of the measurement or generation. Use pause when to specify whether the task pauses above or below this threshold.
